DSH LAUNCH PLANNER — issue #226 task 8.8 part (d), PASS C: launch-root confirmation before publishing, with its 8.10 cases. Branch slice-dsh-planner-d (PR #313), already rebased on main; adopt every commit. Pass B — the planner's argument admission — is delivered on this branch and judged (run dsh-launch-planner-issue-226-tas-10abd37c: no medium-or-higher, no security residual, no spec defect).

THE AUTHORITATIVE TEXT is openspec/changes/2026-09-09-226-session-resumption/tasks.md: task 8.8 from "The remaining launch half of (d) belongs to Pass C" and 8.10's paragraph beginning "Pass C, after B, owns the following DSH stream-json confirmation cases", with design D6 and D7. READ BOTH FIRST and follow them; this commission scopes, it does not restate.

SCOPE.
1. Confirm the launched root BEFORE publishing. The plugin's request-derived session_id alone is never confirmation. Require: a valid prior depth-zero header retained at the resolved locator for the offered ID; the pinned plugin's post-`await agents.resume` init event read from the stream-json child on that selected persistence root; no fresh sibling root or session in the retained store; and new sequence activity past the recorded firstSeq in that same root — all before the launch hold releases. Same-root nonce continuity is 10.7's probe-only device: never planted in a prompt, never read at run time.
2. A missing or different root — followed by a clean exit OR by an otherwise valid delivered result file — ends failed or indeterminate under D7: no root_session, no transcript locator, no launch row, and no cold replacement authorised by itself.
3. The 8.10 Pass C cases, each over a captured SYNTHETIC child transcript with no installed provider: confirmation then current work publishes root_session and the launch row only after the init event; child exits before any init event; init event naming a different root, both endings; nonzero exit with stderr prose but no measured machine-readable session-rejection shape performs no automatic cold replacement; cancellation or deadline expiry while the hold is open fabricates nothing and starts no replacement; and the one DSH-specific local-decline path, an unsupported offer, permits exactly one independently safe cold launch. Label them the DSH arm of LE1/LE3/AS4/D7.
4. Production changes require a demonstrated failing test first. Preserve Pass B's admission and every inherited guard. Prove each production change by removal.

TWO SMALL DEBTS ON THIS BRANCH, in scope because they block its landing:
D1. LOW from run 10abd37c's chief: crates/brokkr-cli/tests/driver_conformance.rs:535-539 infers "no overlay was staged" from a log only the launched shim writes. Observe staging independently of child execution, transient files included, and align the delivery claim in tasks.md with that evidence.
D2. Issue #255, reproduced today on this branch inside the box: adapters::composite::tests::spawn_node_runtime_reads_one_version_line_and_refuses_the_rest failed with "node --version: Text file busy (os error 26)" while the other 387 protocol tests passed. The fixture writes an executable shim and execs it while a writer's descriptor can still be open in a sibling thread's fork. The house fix is staging by RENAME, never retry: write the shim beside its target under a temporary name, close it, then rename it into place before anything execs it. Apply that to this fixture and to any sibling fixture in composite/tests.rs that writes then execs a shim in place. Do not add a retry loop.

OUT OF SCOPE: Pass D's composite/containment/retained-storage matrix, 9.6, 10.x, 11.x, groups 14–15, any live provider call, any new digest producer or public planner seam. Hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063): no Windows handling; canonicalise temp roots; take errno text from the host's io::Error.

GATES for the smith, crate-scoped and sequential: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; each crate's suite on its own; openspec validate --all --strict; both bundle compiles. The recipe's own verify gate runs the workspace suite by design; that is the recipe, not a finding.

DO NOT TICK 8.8 or 8.10 unless their ENTIRE acceptance is met; tick a sub-clause only when its whole acceptance is. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/, extensions/dsh/, docs/decisions/ do not move; 0056 stays proposed; the DSH route stays disabled. Record what you delivered and exactly what Pass D and 9.6 still owe.

which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

result.notes:
Pass C delivered on slice-dsh-planner-d. A new private DshRootWatch in crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs stands between the stream-json child and the launch hold: fold_dsh_stream_event no longer calls LaunchHold::confirm from the request-derived session_id. The hold releases only when four mechanically observable facts agree - the valid prior depth-zero header retained at the resolved locator for the offered id (its pre-spawn half is the boundary owned_dsh_root read off that header; its settle-time half re-selects and requires exactly one), the pinned plugin's post-await agents.resume init event naming that same root, no fresh sibling root or session in the retained store (censused BEFORE the spawn), and new sequence activity past the recorded firstSeq. Until they agree nothing is published: no root_session, no launch row, and no transcript locator - a rejoin now holds the locator beside the launch row instead of recording it before the spawn. settle runs before every drain, so D7's order (location, launch, first work) is asserted directly. dsh_session_file_reading became a filter over a new dsh_depth_zero_sessions_reading so census and selection are two readings of one bounded walk, with every containment, budget, header rule and refusal string unchanged. Nonce continuity stays 10.7's probe-only device.

The 8.10 cases assigned to Pass C are delivered as the DSH arm of LE1/LE3/AS4/D7, each over a captured synthetic child transcript with no installed provider, through production's own invoke_dsh_launch: confirmation then current work (one resumed row with root_session, published only after the init event, in order transcript/harness-started/seat-turn, folding only the current event); the request-derived id alone; child exit before any init; init naming a different root on both endings (clean exit and an otherwise valid delivered result file); the four requirements withheld one at a time plus an ambiguous second header; a nonzero exit with stderr prose performing no automatic cold replacement (spawn counter shows one child); a kill inside the open hold fabricating nothing; and the unsupported offer taking exactly one independently safe cold launch, driven end to end through run_seat over the shipped route. The DSH arm cannot reach run_seat on the QUALIFIED route without an installed provider (the gate resolves real seams and a real composite there), so those cases assert the adapter's own LaunchTerminal and rows, and the shared run_seat unsettled guard behind them stays proven by the existing codex and claude cases. That division is recorded in tasks.md, not papered over.

Six production guards were each removed as a compiling mutation and observed failing at its own assertion, then restored: the prior header's boundary, the init event, the pre-spawn census, the exactly-one-header selection, the sequence advance, and the held locator.

D1 is answered. driver_conformance's 'no overlay was staged' read a log only the launched shim writes. The driver child now gets its own TMPDIR - the seat overlay's home - emptied and stamped into 1990 with POSIX touch -t before each run, so any create or unlink moves the stamp and a transient file is as visible as a surviving one. assert_no_provider_work asserts the stamp did not move; assert_provider_work is the positive control and also asserts nothing was left behind; dsh_overlay_staging_is_observed_without_any_child_execution supplies the shape no shim log can report (a fixture pointed at a dsh that does not exist stages, spawns nothing, cleans up, and the stamp still reports it) beside the negative control on the same fixture. Removal proof: unsetting the child's TMPDIR fails that test and the launch-path proof. The matching delivery claim in tasks.md is corrected to describe exactly this evidence.

D2 is answered, and the commission's prescribed fix was measured wrong before it was replaced - stated plainly here because the record has to be honest. The named fixture ALREADY staged by rename and still failed. execve refuses while the inode's write count is above zero, and rename moves the inode, write count and all, so a destination renamed in inherits exactly the descriptor the staging file carried. Measured on this host, 8 forking threads and 4000 rounds per mode: write in place 436 ETXTBSY, stage-and-rename 471, write the bytes from a CHILD 0. stage_executable (composite/tests.rs), executable (adapters/tests.rs) and make_shim (driver_conformance.rs) now hand their bytes to /bin/sh -c 'cat > "$0"' under the staging child's own PATH, so this process never opens the exec'd inode for writing; the mode is set afterwards by the parent because chmod opens nothing. No retry loop and no sleep was added, and the inherited ETXTBSY retry in a_qualified_stream_json_launch_ends_on_a_non_utf8_line was removed with its cause. spawn_retrying_etxtbsy is untouched: its subject is current_exe, a file no thread of this run writes, so it is neither the repair nor evidence of it. a_renamed_shim_inherits_its_writer_and_a_staged_one_carries_none pins the mechanism deterministically. The protocol lib suite ran clean three times in a row afterwards.

Not ticked: 8.8 and 8.10 stay unchecked and no sub-clause was ticked. Pass D still owes the whole composite/containment/doctor/adaptation-bytes/retained-storage matrix of 8.10 (component drift to unverified-harness, the canonical lock and plugin vectors, profile and optional-extension containment and identity, the outstanding locator/storage matrix); 9.6 still owes full DSH accounting and compatibility (cold and warm retained-store integration, historical versus current multi-message/tool/retry intervals, output/tool/target filtering, usage deduplication, per-message versus cumulative accounting, omission of unattributable totals, legacy behaviour). 10.x, 11.x and groups 14-15 were not opened. contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, policy/schemas/, fixtures/, reference/, extensions/dsh/ and docs/decisions/ have no diff; 0056 stays proposed; the DSH route stays disabled; no live provider call, no new digest producer, no new public planner seam, no Windows handling (0063). Nothing was pushed.

members.correctness:
Read the authoritative 8.8(d)/8.10 Pass C clauses and D6/D7, then reviewed both run commits a760322e..4acb9d42 (cbf99c5e production/tests and 4acb9d42 delivery record), all five changed files, and the adopted Pass B context. No source edits, fixes, commits, live provider calls or security verdict.

R1 MEDIUM — crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs:3995-4003, 4006-4014, 4169-4214: running settle before drain does not ensure confirmation precedes work. settle can return with the hold open, but drain_dsh_transcript still emits current seat-turn/tool rows directly. An ordinary interleaving is: init arrives; settle reads last_seq == first_seq and returns; the child appends a current assistant/message; drain emits seat-turn; the later result event lets settle confirm and emit transcript/harness-started, ending Resumed. Likewise, work drained before a delayed init can later become an accepted rejoin. No DSH path latches that pre-confirmation work as uncertain (the drain does not even pass through LaunchHold::observe). This violates D7's held-facts-before-first-work order and its prohibition on accepting work before required confirmation. Gate/buffer the drain's publication and latch an observed pre-confirmation-work violation; add deterministic tests for a delayed init and an append between settle and drain. The current positive test's final ordering assertion does not control this interleaving. This is a source-traced counterexample, not a claimed reproduced race; 400 repetitions of the existing positive test passed.

R2 MEDIUM — crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/composite/tests.rs:2415-2435: a_renamed_shim_inherits_its_writer_and_a_staged_one_carries_none is cfg(unix), but unconditionally expects executing a script held open for writing to fail with errno 26. That is Linux behavior, not a portable Unix rule. Apple's XNU exec_check_permissions explicitly compiles out the v_writecount/ETXTBSY check (#if 0), so the script can execute on the supported macOS host and output().unwrap_err() fails. Source-backed portability finding, not a claimed native macOS run: https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/kern/kern_exec.c#L6340-L6349 . Restrict the Linux mechanism assertion appropriately and retain a portable successful staging control; verify on macOS.

R3 MEDIUM — crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/tests.rs:5152-5190 and openspec/changes/2026-09-09-226-session-resumption/tasks.md:12854 onward: the claimed cancellation/deadline case only executes kill -TERM $$ inside the provider shim and returns through invoke_dsh_launch. It kills neither the driver nor a process group, creates no deadline, exercises no supported cancellation control, and cannot assert deadline_killed or observe the outer driver's held checkpoints/replacement behavior. It proves a signalled provider exit, not either required 8.10/D7 case. Add actual outer-process cancellation and watchdog-expiry cases over the synthetic DSH init/store exchange, checking no fabricated root/locator/launch or replacement and the preserved deadline outcome; correct the completion claim until these exist.

R4 LOW (fit) — crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/composite/tests.rs:76-107, crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/tests.rs:484-522, crates/brokkr-cli/tests/driver_conformance.rs:932-960: D2 explicitly requires writing a sibling temporary file, closing it, then renaming into place. The replacement helpers instead have a child truncate/write the final pathname and remove the rename. The recorded Linux experiment reasonably motivates a child writer to avoid inherited parent descriptors, but does not require dropping atomic installation. Have that child write the temporary sibling, reap it, then rename; this preserves the measured improvement and the commissioned house rule without a retry.

D1 is correctly addressed: a separate driver TMPDIR timestamp observes transient staging independently of child execution, with positive and negative controls and a corrected delivery account. Independent Linux checks passed: 101 focused protocol DSH tests; all 23 built-CLI driver conformance tests; the named Node-version test; the new ETXTBSY test; git diff --check. Inspected the recorded six removal summaries without replaying mutations. Verify's recorded workspace-suite/self-bundle pass is acknowledged. Frozen trees have no diff against origin/main; 0056 remains proposed, DSH stays disabled, and 8.8/8.10 remain unticked. OpenSpec strict validation, capable-host exact coverage, native macOS and final-head remote CI remain pending as recorded; no gate was waived. Pass D and 9.6 remain outside this review's requested implementation scope.
members.security: Security-only read-only review of a760322e..4acb9d42, including both implementation commits, after reading the authoritative Pass C paragraphs and design D6/D7. SEC-1 (medium): current work can cross the launch hold and then be retroactively accepted as a confirmed rejoin. At crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs:3995-4003, settle can return without confirmation, but drain_dsh_transcript still emits current seat-turn rows directly. DshRootWatch records no work-before-confirmation failure, and its later settle at lines 4163-4214 can publish the locator, launch row and root_session. Source-traced counterexample: with an admitted offered session at firstSeq 27, a synthetic child appends an assistant/message at seq 28, writes {} to stdout, then writes the matching system/init event and exits clean with a valid result. The first JSON event drains seat-turn while the watch is unconfirmed; the subsequent init settles to Resumed, yielding seat-turn before transcript/harness-started. run_seat then skips its unsettled guard at line 5436, allowing successful delivery despite D7 requiring work before confirmation to remain failed or uncertain. The new deferred store check also permits this ordering after an init when a complete current message precedes a temporarily incomplete final transcript row: settle refuses that read, the drain emits the complete message, and a later complete read confirms. This is a fail-closed and journal-attestation gap, not merely a display ordering issue. Prevent unconfirmed work from later becoming an accepted resumed invocation; add a deterministic synthetic regression for this sequence and prove the guard by removal. No high/critical finding established. The DSH route remains disabled, and frozen surfaces have no diff. Fresh validation: cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib --all-features --locked dsh passed 101 tests; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test driver_conformance --all-features --locked dsh passed 5 tests. The counterexample is a source trace, not an executed new regression. No source fixes or commits were made.

result.notes:
Reviewed the authoritative 8.8(d)/8.10 Pass C paragraphs and design D6/D7, both run commits a760322e..4acb9d42, all five changed files and the surrounding admission/launch/terminal paths. Checked the panel's claims against source rather than treating its prose as instructions. The panel's residual/medium floor is preserved. R1 MEDIUM, security residual — authors: correctness R1 and security SEC-1. crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs:3995-4014, 4163-4214; drain at 2088 and terminal guard at 5436. settle may return unconfirmed, but drain_dsh_transcript still publishes current seat-turn/tool rows directly. A child can append assistant/message seq 28 after the retained firstSeq 27, emit {}, then emit the matching init and deliver successfully: the first event drains work without confirmation; the later init publishes transcript/harness-started/root_session and returns Resumed, bypassing run_seat's unsettled-result guard. An append between settle and drain also breaks publication order. No DSH latch preserves work-before-confirmation as uncertain. This violates D7's ordering and refusal to accept pre-confirmation work. Gate publication and permanently reject an observed pre-confirmation-work sequence; prove delayed-init and settle/drain interleavings with deterministic synthetic regressions and guard removal. Confirmed by source trace, not an executed new regression.

R2 MEDIUM — author: correctness R2. crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/composite/tests.rs:2415-2435. The new cfg(unix) test unconditionally expects executing an open-for-write shell script to fail with errno 26. Apple's exec_check_permissions disables that writer-count check, so the Linux assertion is not portable to supported macOS and unwrap_err can fail there. Restrict the mechanism assertion to Linux while preserving the successful staging control on both hosts. Independently checked [Apple XNU source](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/kern/kern_exec.c#L6340-L6349); this is a source-backed portability finding, not a native macOS run.

R3 MEDIUM — author: correctness R3. crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/tests.rs:5152-5190; tasks.md:12854. The claimed cancellation/deadline case only runs kill -TERM $$ in the provider shim through invoke_dsh_launch. It neither cancels the outer driver/process tree nor creates a watchdog deadline, and cannot verify deadline_killed or the driver's held checkpoints. Add the actual DSH synthetic cancellation and deadline-expiry cases required by 8.10/D7, asserting no fabricated root/locator/launch or replacement and preservation of the deadline outcome. Correct the delivery claim until those cases exist.

R4 LOW — author: correctness R4. composite/tests.rs:76-107, adapters/tests.rs:484-522 and crates/brokkr-cli/tests/driver_conformance.rs:932-960.
